name: Linux kernel
review_venue: email to LKML plus subsystem lists; some subsystems run patchwork.kernel.org; archived on lore.kernel.org
issue_tracker: mailing lists per MAINTAINERS (primary); bugzilla.kernel.org used by only a few subsystems; regzbot for regressions
governance: Linus Torvalds has final say over mainline; Greg Kroah-Hartman runs stable. Hierarchical subsystem maintainers. Torvalds and GKH are Linux Foundation fellows. LF Technical Advisory Board; yearly Maintainers Summit.
why: The kernel under nearly all servers, phones and containers; mailing-list regime.

name: GNU C Library
review_venue: mailing list libc-alpha@sourceware.org plus patchwork.sourceware.org (project 'glibc')
governance: GNU project (FSF), run by the glibc stewards and maintainer consensus. Hosted on Sourceware (an SFC member project). Copyright assignment is no longer required: the DCO is accepted from 2021-08-02.
why: C runtime for most Linux userland; top of Debian's runtime graph.

name: systemd
review_venue: GitHub PRs, merged by maintainers (merge, squash, or rebase all allowed); no merge queue
license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (udev parts GPL-2.0-or-later; GitHub reports GPL-2.0)
governance: Independent volunteer and multi-company core team (maintainers employed at Microsoft, Meta, Red Hat, etc.); no foundation. Poettering said in 2015 the project would not become a company or foundation.
why: Init and service manager on most distributions; GitHub-native contrast to the kernel.

name: BusyBox
review_venue: mailing list busybox@busybox.net; ad-hoc GitHub PRs on the mirror since 2026-06 (none merged via GitHub)
issue_tracker: GitHub issues on vda-linux/busybox_mirror (bugs.busybox.net now just says 'Please report bugs on GitHub')
governance: Single maintainer, Denys Vlasenko (BDFL-style). Earlier leads were Bruce Perens, Erik Andersen and Rob Landley. Volunteer project.
why: Userland of Alpine and countless embedded/container images (13B Docker pulls).

name: GCC
review_venue: mailing list gcc-patches@gcc.gnu.org (plus component lists: libstdc++, fortran, ...); patchwork.sourceware.org project 'gcc'; experimental Forgejo PRs on forge.sourceware.org/gcc/gcc
governance: GCC Steering Committee within GNU/FSF; area maintainers listed in MAINTAINERS; heavy corporate participation (Red Hat, SUSE, Arm, Intel, IBM, ...). DCO allowed from 2021-06 alongside FSF assignment.
why: System compiler for most of the free software stack; pairs with LLVM.

name: LLVM / Clang
review_venue: GitHub PRs
license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception (legacy code also NCSA)
governance: Foundation: LLVM Foundation (non-profit) plus community governance (area-team details unverified).
why: Compiler infrastructure behind Clang, Rust, Swift and many JITs; moved review to GitHub PRs in 2023.

name: CMake
review_venue: GitLab MRs; @kwrobot integrates on 'Do: merge'
governance: Company-led (Kitware)
why: De facto C/C++ build system; Kitware GitLab regime.

name: Git
review_venue: mailing list git@vger.kernel.org; GitGitGadget turns GitHub PRs (gitgitgadget/git, git/git) into list patches
issue_tracker: mailing list only (no tracker; 'git bugreport' output goes to the list)
governance: Junio C Hamano has been maintainer since 2005-07. Git is a Software Freedom Conservancy member project with a Project Leadership Committee.
why: Version control under all of the above; mailing-list regime.

name: uv
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Company: Astral Software. On 2026-03-19 Astral announced an agreement to join OpenAI (Codex team), with the tools to stay open source. Whether the deal has closed is unverified: no closing notice was found on astral.sh/blog through 2026-10-27.
why: 2024 entrant: Python package manager with ~128M PyPI downloads/month; tests whether a new backbone looks different.

name: CPython
review_venue: GitHub PRs
license: Python-2.0 (PSF License stack; doc code examples 0BSD)
governance: Foundation: PSF owns the IP; technical governance by the elected Steering Council (PEP 13, since 2019-02).
why: Reference Python; top of Debian's graph and a top-10 Docker image.

name: Node.js
review_venue: GitHub PRs, landed by the commit-queue (GitHub Actions + @node-core/utils) or manually with 'git node land'
license: MIT (GitHub reports NOASSERTION because LICENSE bundles third-party licenses)
governance: OpenJS Foundation (formed 2019-03 from the merger of the Node.js Foundation, est. 2015, and the JS Foundation); TSC-led.
why: Server-side JavaScript runtime; OpenJS Foundation.

name: OpenJDK
review_venue: GitHub PRs driven by Skara bots: jcheck, plus mlbridge, which posts RFR mails to *-dev lists
governance: Company-led: Oracle is the corporate sponsor. OpenJDK Governing Board; contributions need the Oracle Contributor Agreement (OCA).
why: Java platform reference implementation; Skara PRs on GitHub, JBS issues.

name: Go
review_venue: Gerrit CLs. GitHub PRs have been accepted since 2018-02 via GerritBot, which mirrors each PR into a CL.
governance: Company-led (Google Go team; proposal review committee); separate PATENTS grant.
why: Runtime and toolchain of cloud-native infrastructure; Gerrit review.

name: Rust
review_venue: GitHub PRs gated by a custom merge bot: new bors (rust-lang/bors, account rust-bors), with rollups
governance: Rust Project (Leadership Council, teams) plus the Rust Foundation (est. 2021-02) for legal and infrastructure. Mozilla-sponsored before 2021.
why: Compiler of the fastest-growing systems language; Rust Foundation.

name: PHP
review_venue: GitHub PRs. Language changes go through RFCs on wiki.php.net with an internals@ vote.
governance: Community RFC voting among php-src contributors; the PHP Group holds the license; The PHP Foundation (2021-11) funds core developers.
why: Runtime behind a large share of the web (WordPress, Laravel, Symfony).

name: zlib
review_venue: GitHub PRs and issues, plus email (zlib@gzip.org); the maintainer re-applies changes himself
governance: Single maintainer (Mark Adler; Jean-loup Gailly co-author)
why: Most-embedded compression library; tiny, mature, near-single-maintainer.

name: XZ Utils / liblzma
review_venue: GitHub PRs and issues, plus email/IRC; the maintainer usually re-commits patches himself
license: 0BSD (core); some scripts/build files GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1 (see COPYING; exact SPDX expressions unverified)
governance: Volunteer, single maintainer (Lasse Collin)
why: Ubiquitous compression; 2024 backdoor makes maintainer capacity a documented event.

name: libxml2
review_venue: GitLab merge requests
governance: GNOME-hosted volunteer project. Nick Wellnhofer was effectively the sole maintainer until he removed himself on 2025-12-06 (step-down announced 2025-09-15). Iván Chavero and Daniel Garcia Moreno were added 2025-12-10.
why: XML parser in browsers, desktops and language bindings; GNOME GitLab; documented maintainer-burden case.

name: ICU
review_venue: GitHub PRs; each must reference a Jira ticket ICU-NNNNN; CLA via cla-assistant
governance: Consortium: Unicode Consortium ICU Technical Committee (IBM transferred ICU 2016-05)
why: Unicode and locale engine in every major OS and browser; consortium governance.

name: Protocol Buffers
canonical_repo: Google internal monorepo (Piper); public export at https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf
review_venue: GitHub PRs imported by Copybara, reviewed and landed in Google's internal repo, then exported; copybara-service also opens 'test_<CL>' presubmit PRs for internal changes
governance: Google-owned and Google-led; no foundation.
why: Serialization backbone across languages; Google-internal sync (Copybara) regime.

name: OpenSSL
canonical_repo: private committer-only origin; public downstream clone at https://github.com/openssl/openssl
review_venue: GitHub PRs (committer/OTC approvals, then landed by script)
governance: Foundation-led: OpenSSL Foundation and OpenSSL Corporation as co-equal bodies since the 2024-07 restructure (OMC dissolved); Technical Advisory Committees formed 2025-03.
why: Dominant TLS/crypto library; foundation-led since Heartbleed.

name: curl / libcurl
review_venue: GitHub PRs (plus curl-library mailing list)
governance: Volunteer BDFL project (Daniel Stenberg, employed full-time on curl by wolfSSL since 2019); no legal entity and no umbrella foundation.
why: Transfer library in billions of devices; ended its bug bounty over AI slop (Jan 2026).

name: OpenSSH
review_venue: mailing list openssh-unix-dev@mindrot.org plus patches attached in Bugzilla plus GitHub PRs on the mirror
governance: OpenBSD project (Theo de Raadt; OpenBSD Foundation funds it). Portable is maintained by Damien Miller and Darren Tucker.
why: Remote access on essentially every Unix host; OpenBSD-led.

name: libuv
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Maintainer group listed in MAINTAINERS.md; closely tied to Node.js (foundation affiliation unverified).
why: Async I/O loop under Node.js and many runtimes; passes on breadth (high in three channels, dominant in none) — the quiet-engine path.

name: PostgreSQL
review_venue: mailing list pgsql-hackers plus the CommitFest app
issue_tracker: mailing list pgsql-bugs plus web bug form (BUG #nnnnn); no tracker
governance: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, led by the Core Team, with committers and contributors and several community non-profits. No single company controls it.
why: Leading open-source RDBMS (12.4B Docker pulls, all three hyperscalers); mailing-list + commitfest regime.

name: SQLite
review_venue: none for outsiders ('open-source, not open-contribution'); patches need a public-domain affidavit and may be reimplemented; discussion on the SQLite Forum
issue_tracker: SQLite Forum for real-world bugs; separate SQLite Bug Forum for AI-agent, fuzzer and static-analysis reports
governance: Hwaci (Hipp, Wyrick & Company): D. Richard Hipp and a small core team, funded by the SQLite Consortium and support contracts.
why: Most-deployed database engine; Fossil, closed to outside contributions (commit-only regime).

name: Redis
review_venue: GitHub PRs (squash/rebase; merge commits disabled); Redis CLA required
license: LicenseRef-RSALv2 OR SSPL-1.0 OR AGPL-3.0-only (AGPL version suffix not stated explicitly; Redis says 'AGPLv3')
governance: Company-led by Redis Ltd (formerly Redis Labs). antirez was BDFL until stepping back in 2020-06 and rejoined Redis in 2024-12. Contributions require the Redis Software Grant and CLA.
why: Dominant in-memory store; 2024 license change and 2025 return to an OSI license.

name: Valkey
review_venue: GitHub PRs (squash/rebase); DCO sign-off
governance: Linux Foundation project, announced 2024-03-28 with backing from AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson, and Snap, led initially by Madelyn Olson (AWS); open governance with a multi-company TSC (current TSC membership not verified).
why: Design pair with Redis: the 2024 license fork, adopted by AWS and Google Cloud. Fails the gate only because distributions lag.

name: Apache Kafka
review_venue: GitHub PRs, squash-merge only. KIPs on cwiki + dev@ vote for major changes.
governance: Foundation: Apache Software Foundation (PMC); Confluent is a heavy contributor.
why: Event-streaming backbone (all three hyperscalers); ASF with GitHub PRs and Jira.

name: nginx
review_venue: GitHub PRs (rebase merge only)
governance: Company-led by F5 (acquired NGINX Inc. in 2019).
why: Most-pulled Docker image (13.6B); development moved to GitHub in 2024.

name: Apache HTTP Server
review_venue: GitHub PRs for all changes. 2.4.x backports are PRs whose reviews replace STATUS-file votes.
governance: Foundation: Apache Software Foundation (PMC)
why: Apache HTTP Server; SVN-canonical ASF regime and contrast to nginx.

name: Kubernetes
review_venue: GitHub PRs via Prow: /lgtm and /approve labels from OWNERS, merged by Tide (k8s-ci-robot)
governance: CNCF (accepted 2016-03-10, graduated 2018-03-06); SIG and Steering Committee governance; Google-originated.
why: Container orchestration standard; managed by all three hyperscalers.

name: containerd
review_venue: GitHub PRs with GitHub merge queue (merge commit/rebase); 2 maintainer approvals
governance: CNCF (accepted 2017-03-29, graduated 2019-02-28); originated at Docker; multi-company maintainers.
why: Quiet container runtime under Kubernetes and Docker.

name: QEMU
review_venue: mailing list qemu-devel@nongnu.org tracked by patchew; submaintainers send PULL requests by mail; GitLab MRs not accepted
governance: QEMU Leadership Committee; Software Freedom Conservancy member project. Maintainers are mostly corporate (Red Hat, Linaro, IBM, ...).
why: Virtualization/emulation under KVM clouds and CI; mailing-list regime; AI-contribution ban.

name: FFmpeg
review_venue: dual venue: Forgejo PRs at code.ffmpeg.org plus the ffmpeg-devel list with patchwork.ffmpeg.org
issue_tracker: Forgejo issues (primary per doc/issue_tracker.txt, 2026-05) with Trac as legacy
governance: Volunteer community. A General Assembly elects the Technical Committee and Community Committee (structure since about 2020; not re-verified). Funds go through SPI. Michael Niedermayer is the long-time de facto lead. CI is sponsored by GitHub and Blacksmith (2026-11).
why: Media codec engine behind most video software; moved to Forgejo in 2025; AI-found-bug dispute.

name: Mesa 3D
review_venue: GitLab merge requests, merged by Marge-bot
governance: Community project hosted on freedesktop.org (X.Org Foundation umbrella). Contributors are mostly paid engineers (Intel, AMD, Valve, Collabora, Google, Red Hat, Igalia, ...).
why: Open graphics driver stack (OpenGL/Vulkan) on Linux; freedesktop GitLab regime.

name: FreeType
review_venue: GitLab MRs plus freetype-devel@nongnu.org patches
governance: Small volunteer team led by Werner Lemberg; hosted on freedesktop.org.
why: Font rasterizer in Android, ChromeOS, Linux desktops and games.

name: NumPy
review_venue: github_pr
governance: NumFOCUS fiscally sponsored project (sponsorship start date unverified); community Steering Council.
why: Array foundation of scientific Python; anchors the performance phase (asv history).

name: pandas
review_venue: github_pr
governance: NumFOCUS fiscally sponsored since 2015 (pandas About page); core team with a steering committee.
why: Dataframe workhorse; heavy GSO/SWE-fficiency coverage.

name: Matplotlib
review_venue: github_pr
governance: NumFOCUS fiscally sponsored project (start date unverified); community steering council.
why: Reference Python plotting library; in SWE-bench (benchmark-exposed).

name: scikit-learn
review_venue: github_pr
governance: NumFOCUS fiscally sponsored (listed as Sponsored on numfocus.org); community governance document with maintainers and a technical committee. Financially supported by Probabl (Inria spin-off) and others; INRIA holds copyright for work by its employees.
why: Classical ML library; in SWE-bench (benchmark-exposed).

name: Plotly (plotly.js + plotly.py)
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Company: Plotly Technologies Inc.
why: Design pair with matplotlib (benchmark-unexposed plotting); single-channel significance only.

name: D3
canonical_repo: https://github.com/d3/d3; https://github.com/d3/d3-array; https://github.com/d3/d3-axis; https://github.com/d3/d3-brush; https://github.com/d3/d3-chord; https://github.com/d3/d3-color; https://github.com/d3/d3-contour; https://github.com/d3/d3-delaunay; https://github.com/d3/d3-dispatch; https://github.com/d3/d3-drag; https://github.com/d3/d3-dsv; https://github.com/d3/d3-ease; https://github.com/d3/d3-fetch; https://github.com/d3/d3-force; https://github.com/d3/d3-format; https://github.com/d3/d3-geo; https://github.com/d3/d3-hierarchy; https://github.com/d3/d3-interpolate; https://github.com/d3/d3-path; https://github.com/d3/d3-polygon; https://github.com/d3/d3-quadtree; https://github.com/d3/d3-random; https://github.com/d3/d3-scale; https://github.com/d3/d3-scale-chromatic; https://github.com/d3/d3-selection; https://github.com/d3/d3-shape; https://github.com/d3/d3-time; https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format; https://github.com/d3/d3-timer; https://github.com/d3/d3-transition; https://github.com/d3/d3-zoom
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Volunteer/BDFL style. Creator Mike Bostock maintains D3 with Philippe Riviere, both at Observable, Inc. (d3js.org). There is no foundation or formal governance.
why: Benchmark-unexposed JS visualization foundation; browser-side libraries are invisible to distro and container channels. Modular (d3-* repos) — mapping still to do.

name: PyTorch
review_venue: github_pr landed by pytorchmergebot (@pytorchbot merge); ghstack and GitHub-native stacks
governance: Foundation: PyTorch Foundation under the Linux Foundation since 2022-09-12. Technical decisions rest with maintainers (codified technical governance); Meta is the largest contributor.
why: Dominant deep-learning framework; AI-domain stratum (demand confound).

name: Hugging Face Transformers
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Company: Hugging Face, Inc.
why: Model-definition hub of the LLM era; AI-domain stratum.

name: React
review_venue: GitHub PRs, squash-only; core team often uses Sapling stacked PRs
governance: Meta-led until 2026. React Foundation (Linux Foundation) announced 2025-10-07 and launched 2026-02-24; it owns React, React Native, and JSX. Repos moved from the facebook org to the react org around early June 2026 (reported 2026-06-10; PR #36752 on 2026-06-11 updated package.json URLs). Technical governance is a provisional leadership council.
why: Dominant UI library; moved from Meta to the React Foundation (Linux Foundation) in 2026.

name: Vite
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Run by the Vite core team, with no formal governance document on vite.dev/team; Evan You is the creator. VoidZero Inc. (Evan You's company) employed several core members, and VoidZero joined Cloudflare on 2026-06-04. Vite's blog says team governance and the MIT license are unchanged, and Cloudflare added a $1M ecosystem fund administered by the Vite team.
why: 2020 entrant that already passes the main gate; JS build tool.

name: Django
review_venue: github_pr + Trac ticket triage (Unreviewed / Accepted / Ready for checkin)
governance: Foundation: Django Software Foundation (est. 2008) with paid Fellows. Technical direction from the Steering Council and mergers.
why: Python web framework; DSF-governed; in SWE-bench (benchmark-exposed).

name: Spring Framework
review_venue: GitHub PRs, but maintainers usually merge locally (polish, rebase, cherry-pick) and close the PR with 'Closes gh-N'
governance: Company-led: Broadcom (via its 2023-11 acquisition of VMware; Spring team in VMware Tanzu, earlier Pivotal/SpringSource). Moved from CLA to DCO in 2025-01.
why: Backbone of enterprise Java; Broadcom-led.

name: Ruby on Rails
review_venue: github_pr
governance: Rails Core Team (DHH, creator); the Rails Foundation (non-profit, launched 2022-11-14; corporate members including 37signals, Shopify, and GitHub) funds the ecosystem and documentation.
why: Ruby's flagship framework; represents the Ruby ecosystem.
